'''Enéas Ferreira Carneiro''' ({{IPA|pt|eˈnɛ(jj)ɐs feˈʁejɾɐ kaʁˈnejɾu|lang}}; November 5, 1938 — May 6, 2007) was a Brazilian polymath, cardiologist,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www2.camara.leg.br/deputados/pesquisa|title=Quem são|website=Portal da Câmara dos Deputados|language=pt-br|access-date=24 November 2018}}</ref> physicist, mathematician, professor, writer, military serviceman and politician.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www2.camara.leg.br/agencia/noticias/102558.html|title=Saiba mais sobre a vida de Enéas|website=www2.camara.leg.br|access-date=24 November 2018}}</ref><ref name=":5" /> He represented the state of [[São Paulo (state)|São Paulo]] in the [[Chamber of Deputies of Brazil|National Chamber of Deputies]] (the lower house of the [[National Congress of Brazil|National Congress]]) and ran for [[President of Brazil|presidency]] three times. He was founder and leader of the [[Nationalism|nationalist]]<ref>{{Cite book|title=State Crisis in Fragile Democracies: Polarization and Political Regimes in South America|last=Handlin|first=Samuel|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=2017|isbn=978-1108415422|pages=126}}</ref> and conservative<ref>{{Cite book|title=The political right in postauthoritarian Brazil : elites, institutions, and democratization|last=Power|first=Timothy J.|date=2000|publisher=Pennsylvania State University Press|isbn=978-0585380889|location=University Park, Pa.|oclc=48140088}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://archive.boston.com/news/globe/obituaries/articles/2007/05/07/eneas_carneiro_ran_for_president_in_brazil/?rss_id=Boston+Globe+--+Obituaries|title=Eneas Carneiro; ran for president in Brazil – The Boston Globe|website=Boston Globe|access-date=24 November 2018}}</ref> [[Party of the Reconstruction of the National Order]] (PRONA), which was usually seen as being [[Far-right politics|far-right]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://br.geocities.com/eneaspresidente/istoe.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070312050202/http://br.geocities.com/eneaspresidente/istoe.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 12, 2007|title=Entrevista – Revista Isto é|date=March 12, 2007|access-date=January 22, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/portuguese/brasil-40833881|title=O retorno de Enéas, ícone da extrema-direita e 'herói' de Bolsonaro|first=João|last=Fellet|date=August 7, 2017|newspaper=BBC News Brasil|access-date=January 22, 2019|publisher=BBC}}</ref> Although Enéas rejected the [[Left–right political spectrum|left-right dichotomy]], as they were "sides of the same coin", defining himself only as a nationalist.<ref name=":3">Enéas in an interview on the program Jogo do Poder - 1998 - TV Manchete - Journalist Carlos Chagas</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Folha de S.Paulo - Enéas quer retomar estatais privatizadas - 20/04/98 |url=https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/fsp/brasil/fc20049818.htm |access-date=2025-10-21 |website=www1.folha.uol.com.br}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{cite web|access-date=17 October 2021 |author=Odilon Caldeira Neto |date=1 July 2019 |publisher=Café História |title=Enéas Carneiro em dois tempos: do "voto cacareco" a um dos heróis da "nova direita" |url=https://www.cafehistoria.com.br/eneas-carneiro-em-dois-tempos/}}<!-- auto-translated from Portuguese by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

== Biography ==
Eneás Ferreira Carneiro was born in [[Rio Branco, Acre]], located in Brazil's far west, in 1938, under extreme poverty. His parents were the [[barber]] Eustáquio José Carneiro and the [[housewife]] Mina Ferreiro Carneiro.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Conheça a biografia de Enéas Carneiro |url=http://noticias.terra.com.br:80/brasil/noticias/0,,OI1596390-EI7896,00-Conheca+a+biografia+de+Eneas+Carneiro.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200217054016/http://noticias.terra.com.br:80/brasil/noticias/0,,OI1596390-EI7896,00-Conheca+a+biografia+de+Eneas+Carneiro.html |archive-date=2020-02-17 |access-date=2026-02-07 |work=Terra |language=pt-br}}</ref> Eustáquio Carneiro passed away when Eneás was nine years old, prompting him to [[Child labour|start working]] from this young age.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Brasil perde Dr. Enéas Carneiro |url=http://www.partidodarepublica.org.br/partido/NOTICIAS_REPUBLICANAS_2007/noticias_2007_545.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190214191107/http://www.partidodarepublica.org.br/partido/NOTICIAS_REPUBLICANAS_2007/noticias_2007_545.html |archive-date=2019-02-14 |access-date=2026-02-07 |website=www.partidodarepublica.org.br}}</ref> With an slightly improved financial condition, Eneás and his mother moved to [[Belém]] and started living in a shack eating [[flour]] and [[coffee]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Folha de S.Paulo - Cardiologista admira Fidel - 16/10/1994 |url=https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/fsp/1994/10/16/brasil/43.html |access-date=2026-02-07 |website=www1.folha.uol.com.br}}</ref>

Eneás was married to Jamile Augusta Ferreira, a fellow student of the [[School of Medicine and Surgery of the Federal University of the State of Rio de Janeiro|School of Medicine and Surgery of Rio de Janeiro]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Folha de S.Paulo - Candidato tem 3 filhas de mulheres diferentes - 28/8/1994 |url=https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/fsp/1994/8/28/caderno_especial/46.html |access-date=2026-02-07 |website=www1.folha.uol.com.br}}</ref> The couple had one daughter, Janete, after both finished their studies at the School of Medicine. Five years later, Eneás had another daughter, Gabriela, with his union with the [[Speech–language pathology|speech therapist]] Selene Maria. This relationship was also not long-running. Eneás, around 1982, married the prosecutor Adriana Lorandi, having his third daughter, Lígia. The third marriage of Enéas was also not long, since the cardiologist had to give away much property to create [[Party of the Reconstruction of the National Order|PRONA]].<ref name=":4" />

== Educational career ==
In 1958, Enéas begun his studies at the Army's School of Medicine, Rio de Janeiro. In the next year, graduated as [[third sergeant]], auxiliary of [[anesthesiology]], being the first of his class. At 1960, Carneiro enrolled in the [[School of Medicine and Surgery of Rio de Janeiro]].<ref name=":5" />

In February 1962, Enéas took the [[Entrance examination|entrance exam]] for the Faculty of Philosophy, Science and Letters of the University of the State of Guanabara (nowadays, the [[Rio de Janeiro State University|UERJ]]). He was approved first place in two of his desired courses (physics and mathematics), and started to give classes in the same year on these areas for other students preparing for entrance exams.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Currículo do Dr. Enéas |url=http://prona56.br.tripod.com/cur.eneas.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241208163823/http://prona56.br.tripod.com/cur.eneas.htm |archive-date=2024-12-08 |access-date=2026-02-09 |website=prona56.br.tripod.com}}</ref>

Three years later, Carneiro finished his degree in medicine and asked to be [[Military discharge|discharged]] from the Central Army Hospital after helping in more than 5000 anesthesias and receiving the [[Marechal Hermes Medal]].<ref name=":5" />

Another three years later, in 1968, he finished his degrees in mathematics and physics, founding the Gradiente Course for university exams preparation. In his course, he taught mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and Portuguese. In the next year, Carneiro enrolled in a specialization course in [[cardiology]] at the [[Rio de Janeiro House of Mercy]].<ref name=":5" />

Between 1973 and 1975, he enrolled and finished a [[master's degree]] on cardiology at the [[Federal University of Rio de Janeiro]] while teaching physiology and cardiovascular semiology at the same university. At the same year of his master's degree end, he ministered the first version of his course ''O Eletrocardiograma'' (''The [[Electrocardiography|Electrocardiogram]])'' at Rio de Janeiro, being ministed in the next years at [[São Paulo]] (1983), [[Quito]] (1985) and Rio (1986) as a nationwide course, at the [[Copacabana Palace]] hotel.<ref name=":5" />

After defending his master's dissertation in 1976, he wrote his seminal work ''O Eletrocardiograma'', publishing its first edition in 1977 with the second edition arriving ten years later as ''O Eletrocardiograma: 10 anos depois'' (''The Electrocardiogram: 10 years later''). ''O Eletrocardiograma'' is considered a reference work in cardiology in the Portuguese language, jokingly called the "Enéas' Bible".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2008-04-01 |title=Diário da Câmara dos Deputados, 2008-04-01 |url=http://imagem.camara.gov.br/Imagem/d/pdf/DCD01ABR2008.pdf}}</ref><ref name=":5" />

Despite having been commonly referred as ''Doutor Enéas'' (''Doctor Enéas''), Enéas never defended a doctorate thesis. His unofficial "title" was assigned to him because of his medical occupation and his cult of personality.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Quem é doutor? |url=https://portal.cfm.org.br/artigos/quem-e-doutor/ |access-date=2026-02-09 |website=Portal Médico |language=pt-BR}}</ref>

== Political career ==
In 1989, he established [[PRONA]]. In that [[1989 Brazilian presidential election|same year, he ran for the presidency]] in Brazil's first direct elections after the end of [[History of Brazil#Military rule|military rule]]. Under the electoral laws, every candidate was given a daily amount of free airtime to set out their agenda. Because airtime was proportional to the candidate's party's size, PRONA received roughly 15 seconds of airtime per TV appearance. Nevertheless, he made the most of the opportunity. His exotic image—he was a small, [[Hair loss|bald man]] with a large beard and "coke-bottle" (informal term for thick lens) glasses—drew attention, as did his inflamed speech. In what would become his trademark, he finished it with the catchphrase "{{lang|pt|meu nome é Enéas}}" ('my name is Enéas')—perhaps as gesture of humility or informality, or perhaps a way to save time. The previously unknown candidate placed 12th out of 21 candidates.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Padrão Enéas volta ao horário eleitoral em 2016 |url=https://exame.com/brasil/padrao-eneas-volta-ao-horario-eleitoral-em-2016/ |access-date=2025-12-06 |website=Exame |language=pt-br}}</ref> He got 360,578 votes.

He returned in [[1994 Brazilian general election|1994]], making use then of 1 minute and 17 seconds. Surprising political experts, he finished ahead of various established politicians, such as the then-governor of [[Rio de Janeiro (state)|Rio de Janeiro]] ([[Leonel Brizola]]), the former governor of [[São Paulo]] ([[Orestes Quércia]]), and the then-governor of [[Santa Catarina (state)|Santa Catarina]] ([[Esperidião Amin]]), with more than 4.6&nbsp;million votes.<ref name=":0" />

In [[1998 Brazilian general election|1998]], Enéas got 35 seconds – less, in total airtime, than what he had in 1989 – to deliver a speech that was more nationalistic than ever. Its ideas, such as the construction of an [[atomic bomb]], [[nationalization]] of Brazil's mineral resources, and an increase in the [[Military of Brazil|military]] budget, sparked controversy. According to him, with such an apparatus, Brazil could advance its interests at the UN and in other international treaties.<ref name=":0" /> He got 1.4&nbsp;million votes.

His project focused basically on education, believing that only a strong, interventionist, and technical State would solve Brazil's problems. Although many may label him an authoritarian, his political approach is similar to that of social democracy, as in Sweden and Finland, for example, where the State is extremely important.<ref name=":1" />

In 2000, he ran for mayor of the city of [[São Paulo]], with no success, but he still managed to gain votes for the election of his councilman candidate, [[Havanir Nimtz]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Folha Online - Brasil - Dra. Havanir deixa o Prona e se filia ao PSDB - 02/02/2005 |url=https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/folha/brasil/ult96u67000.shtml |access-date=2025-12-06 |website=www1.folha.uol.com.br}}</ref>

In [[2002 São Paulo gubernatorial election|2002]], he ran for a seat as a federal deputy representing São Paulo and secured the most votes ever for that office. His party won enough votes under the proportional representation system to elect five more deputies.<ref name=":0" />

Enéas also actively participated in the 2004 elections for mayors and council members, helping to choose council members in major cities such as Rio and São Paulo, and mayors in small cities.<ref name=":0" />

In 2006, he was elected again as a federal deputy for São Paulo, this time with the third-highest vote in the state.<ref name=":0" />

== Praise and criticism ==
Many saw Enéas as an exotic politician because of his direct criticism to Brazilians fraudulent politicians behavior.  Enéas believed that by acting on TV what he called "the rage of the common citizen" would wake up Brazilian people against corrupt politicians.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/user/EneasTV|title=YouTube|via=YouTube|access-date=January 22, 2019}}</ref>

== Death and legacy ==
[[File:Deputado federal Enéas Ferreira Carneiro.jpg|thumb|upright|Carneiro in December 2006, five months before his death. He shaved off his signature beard before undergoing treatment against myeloid leukemia.]]
Enéas underwent [[chemotherapy]] at the Hospital Samaritano for [[myeloid leukemia]]. When it became clear that his treatment was not resulting in improvements, he decided to return home, where he remained until his death. Enéas died on May 6, 2007, at approximately 2&nbsp;pm, at 68 years old, in the [[Laranjeiras]] neighborhood of southern Rio de Janeiro. His remains were cremated at the Rio de Janeiro [[Santa Casa da Misericórdia|House of Mercy]]'s crematory and his ashes scattered over the [[Bay of Guanabara]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://g1.globo.com/Noticias/Politica/0,,MUL32252-5601,00.html|title=G1 > Política – Morre o deputado federal Enéas Carneiro|website=g1.globo.com|language=pt-br|access-date=24 November 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/folha/brasil/ult96u91951.shtml|title=Folha Online – Brasil – Morre no Rio o deputado federal Enéas Carneiro – 06/05/2007|website=folha.uol.com.br|access-date=24 November 2018}}</ref>

After his death, on May 8, 2007, Enéas was honored in a [[Anti-abortion movements|rally against abortion]] in [[Brasília]], on May 8, 2007. According to the [[Liberal Party (Brazil, 2006)|Party of the Republic]], the politician was one of the organizers of the event.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/fsp/brasil/fc0805200709.htm|title=Folha de S.Paulo – Memória: Enéas receberá homenagem em ato contra aborto – 08/05/2007|website=folha.uol.com.br|access-date=24 November 2018}}</ref>

In 2017, then-deputy and later President of Brazil [[Jair Bolsonaro]] proposed a bill to include Enéas' name in the [[Tancredo Neves Pantheon of the Fatherland and Freedom|Book of National Heroes]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.camara.gov.br/proposicoesWeb/fichadetramitacao?idProposicao=2138858|title=Projetos de Lei e Outras Proposições – Inscreve o nome de Éneas Ferreira Carneiro no Livro dos Heróis da Pátria|website=camara.gov.br|language=pt-br|access-date=24 November 2018}}</ref> Another bill proposing Eneás to be declared the Brazilian patron of electrocardiography was approved in the [[Chamber of Deputies (Brazil)|lower house]], but archived in the [[Federal Senate (Brazil)|senate]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-02-04 |title=Senado arquiva homenagem a Enéas Carneiro |url=https://colunaesplanada.blogosfera.uol.com.br/2015/02/04/senado-arquiva-homenagem-a-eneas-carneiro/ |access-date=2026-02-09 |website=Política |language=pt-BR}}</ref>
